### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**34** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **9** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **1** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b76df9a6980d935c194f778e7eb10aca382aac4c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `bb112f7f0cefa9c9c944646c739f107ff308fee8` — the merge of head `e28dc246ef66850e593c4e90af4727ff58c60af9` into base `b76df9a6980d935c194f778e7eb10aca382aac4c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin bb112f7f0cefa9c9c944646c739f107ff308fee8 && git checkout bb112f7f0cefa9c9c944646c739f107ff308fee8
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b76df9a6980d935c194f778e7eb10aca382aac4c e28dc246ef66850e593c4e90af4727ff58c60af9 && git checkout -B drift-repro b76df9a6980d935c194f778e7eb10aca382aac4c && git merge --no-ff e28dc246ef66850e593c4e90af4727ff58c60af9

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b76df9a6980d935c194f778e7eb10aca382aac4c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `41dbee6f27bca8c1889c542f0d4a3839e965992a`

### ① Derived judgments

The `Clause-②: yes (widening)` line on the PR body and changeset is true and complete against the diff. New CLI flags `--effort`, `--author-effort` and `--ask-effort` reach `objectstack-scenarios run` / `run-scenarios` through `runner/cli.ts` `main`; `CliArgs`, `DriverEfforts` and `makeDriver`'s widened options stay inside `cli.ts`, which `./runner` does not re-export, so they are no package surface. New exports `CLAUDE_EFFORT_ENV` and `effortLevelsFromHelp` reach `./runner` through `export * from './driver.js'`. Every new field on an exported type is optional (`ClaudeCodeDriverOptions`, `ExternalDriverOptions`, `DriverInfo`, `ExternalLimits`, `TurnProcess`, `TurnSummary`, `HalfScores.build.author`) except `ModelTally.requestedEfforts`, which the scorecard itself builds; it is an output the package produces, not an input a caller writes, so a reader only gains a field. The answer that moves is declared: a live `claude` turn now carries `--effort` when one is asked for, the caller's `CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL` is folded into `--effort` and removed from every turn's environment (measured: the CLI lets it win over the flag), and a level the CLI's own `--help` does not list is refused before any card runs (measured: the CLI only warns and runs at its default). With no flag and no variable set, the argv and environment are as before. `--driver codex` and `--driver recorded:` refuse the three flags; `external:` passes `limits.effort`.

`TurnProcess.requestedEffort` in `transcript.ts` sits outside the order's listed file surface. It is type-only, beside `requestedModel`, and needed for the driver to stamp the field the summary reads. The seat accepts the deviation.

### ② Semver level

Patch, as the changeset bumps it. `Metadata-protocol: none` holds: nothing a metadata author writes (spec, app metadata) is added, narrowed or changed in meaning; the widening is additive flags, exports and fields of the evaluation package `@objectstack/scenarios`, and no existing export is removed, renamed or narrowed in type.

### ③ Boundary flags

None. No `packages/spec/src/**`, no governed path, no runtime or security behaviour of the platform. The turn environment still drops every API-billing variable (`subscriptionOnlyEnv`); the one added removal is the effort variable. The `--help` probe runs the same binary with the same stripped environment. The grader is untouched and stays deterministic (cloud#3600 cost ruling).
